propositions: A scoped sync --only LIVE pass with a bound-issue scalar UPDATE drops the write when the mutation target (jira_key) is not in the selection ids (local ids only), causing remote to stay None and the rendered description to appear empty.

The planner's _scope_excluded scope check compares jira-key-targeted updates against a selection containing only local ids, incorrectly classifying in-scope bound-issue updates as scope_deferred instead of mutate, so the live coordinator+fuse reroute skips the write.

The legacy --filter-local-ids route works because _build_filter_target_set expands scope to LOCAL IDS ∪ BOUND JIRA KEYS, allowing bound-issue updates to be recognized and applied; the primary sync --only route never got this expansion.

A bound-issue update is dropped on every sync --only pass because remote never receives the write, causing outbound_differ to perpetually re-derive the description mismatch and re-emit (symptom 2), and renderedFields to render empty (symptom 1).

The defect was introduced when the coordinator+fuse reroute became authoritative for non-create mutations without ensuring in-scope bound-issue updates are classified as mutate, activating a latent scope-check defect that only fed parity comparison before.

The fix expands selection ids in run_differs to LOCAL IDS ∪ their BOUND JIRA KEYS via pure helper _scoped_selection_ids, so bound-issue updates are recognized in-scope and planned mutate, restoring parity with the legacy route and allowing the write to execute.
